text: An occupant limit is not decoration, and not about comfort. It is arithmetic tied to the exits.
provenance: An occupant limit is not a fire-safety decoration and it is not about comfort.
It is arithmetic tied to the exits.

text: You take the width of the ways out, how fast people move through an opening that wide, how long the building stays survivable, and work back to how many may be inside.
provenance: You take the width of the ways out, you take how fast people move through an opening of that width, you take how long the building will stay survivable, and you work backwards to how many people may be inside.

text: The limit is a statement about the doors. If the doors do not change, the number cannot honestly change either.

text: A fire department memorandum dated the thirtieth of December, 1999 put the occupant load at two hundred and fifty-three.

text: The same memorandum allowed the occupancy to increase to three hundred and seventeen, by removing tables and chairs from three lounge areas.

text: Read that mechanism carefully, because it is reasonable. Tables and chairs take floor space. Remove them and more people fit.

text: If the constraint is floor area, removing furniture genuinely does let you hold more people, and raising the number is correct.
